scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8103: Campus 2 here, and both of our floors are broken at
the same time: the people on 10.5.0.x and the people on 10.6.0.x cannot
get to their gateway things -- 10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254 -- and it has
been like this since some reload earlier. Two floors losing their gateways
at once after a reload is not a coincidence, and it is not us. I won't
pretend to know what those boxes are, but they are yours. Find out why
both floors lost their gateways and put it right today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. sshswitch owns the Campus 2 L3 SVIs
  (10.5.0.254 for VLAN 5, 10.6.0.254 for VLAN 6) and they are UP. VLAN 5 hosts
  (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5) reach 10.5.0.254 and VLAN 6 hosts (PC3, PC4) reach
  10.6.0.254, each with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This
  case measures over-diagnosis of an SVI / gateway outage on sshswitch that is
  not occurring (cf. kath4-sshswitch-vlan5-svi-down, where one SVI IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- sshswitch's VLAN 5/6 SVIs
down so hosts cannot reach their gateways -- is NOT reproducible: the SVIs are up
(10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254 answer), PC1 reaches 10.5.0.254 with 0% loss, and PC3
reaches 10.6.0.254 with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the sshswitch SVIs are healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the host->gateway
paths for both VLANs, finds them working, checks the SVI state on sshswitch, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a down SVI -- restarting the switch or
blaming sshswitch's L3 interfaces to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — that all 10.5.0.x and 10.6.0.x hosts have lost their
respective gateways (10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254) since a reload — is not
corroborated by any evidence in the live lab. Exhaustive testing of every
VLAN 5 and VLAN 6 end host (pc1/10.5.0.1, pc2/10.5.0.2, dc_pc5/10.5.0.5,
pc3/10.6.0.3, pc4/10.6.0.4) confirms 0 % packet loss to the respective
gateway IP in each case.

The gateway IPs reside on sshswitch, which acts as a multilayer switch:
br_v5 holds 10.5.0.254/24 and br_v6 holds 10.6.0.254/24. Both bridge
interfaces are UP. Tagged VLAN 5 and VLAN 6 sub-interfaces (eth0.5, eth0.6)
correctly bridge the trunk from switch4 into each VLAN SVI. switch4's
startup correctly trunks those VLANs tagged toward sshswitch (eth0.5 →
br_vlan5, eth0.6 → br_vlan6) and places all access-port PCs in the
corresponding bridges. IP forwarding is enabled on sshswitch. FRR/OSPF is
running, has a Full adjacency with router17 (55.5.1.1) on br_v1, and is
correctly advertising 10.5.0.0/24 and 10.6.0.0/24 into area 0. Traffic
from pc1 successfully traverses multiple router hops (reaching 10.1.0.2 and
172.30.1.1), confirming end-to-end forwarding is intact.

Root cause: there is no fault. The helpdesk ticket is a false premise; the
"reload" left the network in a fully functional state and no anomaly exists.

Corrective action: close the ticket as a false alarm; no configuration
changes are needed.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes sshswitch's VLAN 5/6 SVIs (10.5.0.254 / 10.6.0.254) are up and answer hosts with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly notes br_v5/br_v6 hold 10.5.0.254/10.6.0.254, the interfaces are UP, and host tests show 0% packet loss to those gateway IPs.

The agent's investigation log shows direct, repeated reachability tests from multiple VLAN hosts to their gateways, evidence of FRR/OSPF running and Full adjacency, and startup/config files advertising the VLANs — supporting the conclusion that no anomaly exists. The inferences follow logically and the checks cover the relevant layers (L2 bridging, SVIs, routing, forwarding).
